question: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:
Possibility of introducing a shortcut for the recognition of midwives’ professional qualifications in the context of Directive 2005/36/EC

Poland is seeing the progressive closure of obstetric and gynaecological units, leading to thousands of highly qualified midwives losing their jobs. At the same time, the Polish healthcare system is suffering from chronic shortages of nursing staff. Midwives have extensive skills acquired during their studies and many years of professional practice, including in the departments of surgery, general medicine, anaesthetics and intensive care, and have also completed postgraduate courses in surgical and anaesthetic nursing. Nevertheless, they face barriers to these qualifications being recognised in other branches. In connection to this: 1.

Is the Commission considering the possibility of amending Article 31 of Directive 2005/36/EC by adding an additional shortened training route (bridge studies) enabling midwives to obtain a qualification as a nurse responsible for general care, taking into account ECTS credits and professional experience?

What action is the Commission taking to facilitate the recognition of partial qualifications and professional experience acquired in the health sector, particularly in the context of staff shortages in the Member States?
Does the Commission plan to carry out an analysis of the impact that possible changes to the directive may have on patient safety and the professional mobility of healthcare professionals?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) Directive 2005/36/EC1 sets minimum training requirements for accessing the profession of nurse responsible for general care across the EU. Under the Directive2, bridges between different health professional careers paths can be set at national level for equivalent training in terms of content and level to the ones required for nurse training. Health workforce shortages are a major challenge, requiring action in line with the division of competences in the EU. The organisation of education systems3 and the management of health services4, including adequate staffing, are Member States’ responsibility. EU acquis56 aims to facilitate mobility by ensuring recognition of EU professional qualifications7 and by harmonising minimum training requirements for five health professions8. Under the Directive, Member States may grant full or partial exemption on the basis of a case-by-case assessment via academic recognition to professionals wishing to change or evolve in their professional career path. The upcoming Skills Portability Initiative9 aims, under its Actions 2 and 3, at modernising and speeding up the processes for recognition of professional qualifications for EU citizens and introducing common rules on recognition to attract talent from third countries10. An impact assessment will accompany those initiatives to quantify its impact, notably on the mobility of professionals and how it will be facilitated. However, under these initiatives, the Commission does not intend to modify any of the minimum training requirements for health professions which are provided under the Directive.
1 Directive 2005/36/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 7 September 2005 on the recognition

of professional qualifications (latest consolidated version from 29 October 2025 available here: https://eurlex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A02005L0036-20251029). 2 Article 31(3) of Directive 2005/36/EC. 3 Article 165(1) of the Treaty on the functioning of the European Union. 4 Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the functioning of the European Union. 5 Directive 2005/36/EC on the recognition of professional qualifications. 6 In addition, the Council Recommendation on micro-credentials lists recommendations how to issue, design and deliver micro-credentials (records of the learning outcomes that a learner has acquired following a small volume of learning in formal, non-formal and informal learning). 7 Member States may grant full or partial exemption on the basis of individual assessment. 8 Doctors (and certain medical specialisations), dentists (and certain dental specialties), nurses responsible for general care, midwives and pharmacists under Directive 2005/36/EC. 9 https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/15892-Skills-portability-action-1facilitating-worker-mobility-across-the-EU-through-skills-transparency-and-digitalisation_en. 10 https://employment-social-affairs.ec.europa.eu/news/commission-seeks-views-skills-portability-initiative2025-12-05_en.
